bookInfo.name: Old History of the Five Dynasties

title.zh: 卷十一 梁書11: 后妃列傳一
title.en: Volume 11 Book of Later Liang 11: Biographies 1 - Empresses and Consorts
title.raw: 卷十一 梁書11: 后妃列傳一 Volume 11 Book of Later Liang 11: Biographies 1 - Empresses and Consorts

sentences.zh: 文惠皇太后王氏，開平初追諡。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenhui, née Wang, was given a posthumous title at the beginning of Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenhui (Wang) received her posthumous title early in the Kaiping era.

sentences.zh: 太祖性孝願，奉太后未嘗小失色，朝夕視膳，為士君子之規範。

translations.literal: The Founder by nature was filial and reverent; in serving the Empress Dowager he never once showed the slightest lapse of countenance, morning and evening attending her meals—a model for gentlemen and scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was deeply filial: he never let his manner slip before the Empress Dowager and attended her at every meal, morning and night—a standard for the cultivated man.

sentences.zh: 帝嚴察用法，無纖毫假貸，太后言之，帝頗為省刑。

translations.literal: The Emperor was strict in investigation and application of law, granting not the slightest indulgence; when the Empress Dowager spoke of it, the Emperor considerably lightened punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor enforced the law without mercy; when the Empress Dowager intervened, he often eased sentences.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《北夢瑣言》云：梁祖父誠蚤卒，有三子俱幼。

translations.literal: (《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 says: The Liang Founder’s father Cheng died young, leaving three sons all still young.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 records that the Liang founder’s father Cheng died early, with three sons still small.

sentences.zh: 母王氏，攜養寄於同縣人劉崇家。

translations.literal: The mother, née Wang, took them to be raised and lodged with Liu Chong of the same county.
translations.idiomatic: Their mother Wang entrusted the boys to Liu Chong, a man of the same county.

sentences.zh: 昆弟之中，惟溫狡猾無行，崇母撫養之，崇兄弟嘗加譴杖。

translations.literal: Among the brothers, only Wen was cunning and without proper conduct; Chong’s mother raised him, and Chong’s brothers sometimes beat him with rods.
translations.idiomatic: Of the brothers only Wen was sly and unruly; Liu Chong’s mother cared for him, while Chong’s brothers often thrashed him.

sentences.zh: 一日，偷崇家釜而竄，為崇追回，崇母遮護，以免撲責。

translations.literal: One day he stole a cauldron from Chong’s house and fled; Chong caught him and brought him back, but Chong’s mother shielded him so he escaped a beating.
translations.idiomatic: Once he stole a pot from the Chong household and ran; caught and dragged back, he was spared the rod only because Chong’s mother stood between him and punishment.

sentences.zh: 善逐走鹿，往往及而獲之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at chasing running deer and often overtook and caught them.
translations.idiomatic: He could run down deer on foot and usually brought them down.

sentences.zh: 又，崇母常見其有龍蛇之異。

translations.literal: Moreover, Chong’s mother often saw in him omens of dragons and serpents.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong’s mother also claimed to see dragon-and-serpent portents about him.

sentences.zh: 他日與仲兄存入黃巢軍作賊，伯兄昱與母王氏尚依劉家。

translations.literal: Another day he and his second brother Cun joined Huang Chao’s army as bandits; the eldest brother Yu and their mother Wang still relied on the Liu household.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wen and his second brother Cun went off with Huang Chao’s rebels; the eldest, Yu, and Mother Wang remained with the Lius.

sentences.zh: 溫既辭去，不知存亡。

translations.literal: Once Wen had left, none knew whether he lived or died.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen departed, his fate was unknown.

sentences.zh: 及溫領鎮於汴，盛飾輿馬，使人迎母於崇家。

translations.literal: When Wen held command at Bian, he lavishly adorned carriage and horses and sent men to welcome his mother from Chong’s house.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen became military governor at Bian, he sent a splendid escort to bring his mother from the Chong home.

sentences.zh: 王氏惶恐，辭避深藏，不之信，謂人曰：「朱三落拓無行，何處作賊送死，焉能自致富貴？

translations.literal: Wang was terrified, declined, and hid deep away, not believing it, and said to people: "Zhu Third is shiftless and without conduct—where is he playing bandit and courting death, that he could enrich himself and rise to nobility?
translations.idiomatic: Wang was afraid, refused, and hid; she told others: "That good-for-nothing Zhu Third is off robbing somewhere—how could he possibly have become rich and powerful?

sentences.zh: 汴帥非吾子也。

translations.literal: The Bian commander is not my son."
translations.idiomatic: The lord of Bian cannot be my boy."

sentences.zh: 」使者具陳離鄉去裏之由，歸國立功之事，王氏方泣而信。

translations.literal: The messenger fully set forth the reasons for leaving home and native place and the deeds of returning to the state and achieving merit; only then did Wang weep and believe.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy explained how Wen had left home, served the dynasty, and won distinction; at last Wang wept and believed.

sentences.zh: 是日，與崇母並迎歸汴。

translations.literal: That day she and Chong’s mother were both welcomed back to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The same day both mothers were brought to Bian.

sentences.zh: 溫盛禮郊迎，人士改觀。

translations.literal: Wen received them with grand rites at the suburban greeting; gentlemen changed their view of him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen met them with full suburban ceremony, and onlookers saw him in a new light.

sentences.zh: 崇以舊恩，位至列卿，為商州刺史。

translations.literal: Chong, because of old kindness, rose to rank among chief ministers and became prefect of Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For past kindness to the family, Chong rose to a chief-ministerial post and served as prefect of Shang.

sentences.zh: 王氏以溫貴，封晉國太夫人。

translations.literal: Because Wen had become noble, Wang was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: With Wen’s rise, Wang was created Grand Lady of Jin.

sentences.zh: 仲兄存，於賊中為矢石所中而卒。

translations.literal: The second brother Cun, in the bandit army, was struck by arrow and stone and died.
translations.idiomatic: The second brother Cun died in the rebel ranks, killed by missile weapons.

sentences.zh: 溫置酒於母，歡甚，語及家事，謂母曰：「朱五經辛苦業儒，不登一命，今有子為節度使，無忝前人矣！

translations.literal: Wen set out wine for his mother, very merry, and speaking of family affairs said to her: "Zhu Five Classics toiled at Confucian learning yet never received a single appointment; now I have a son who is military commissioner—no disgrace to our forebears!
translations.idiomatic: At a feast for his mother Wen grew merry and said: "Father Zhu Five Classics studied the classics in poverty and never won office—yet his son is now a military commissioner. We have not shamed our ancestors!

sentences.zh: 」母不懌，良久謂溫曰：「汝致身及此，信為英特，行義未必如先人。

translations.literal: " His mother was displeased and after a long while said to Wen: "You have reached this station—truly you are extraordinary—but in conduct you surely do not match your forebears.
translations.idiomatic: " His mother was unmoved and after a pause told Wen: "You have risen high—no doubt you are gifted—but your conduct is hardly like your father’s.

sentences.zh: 朱二與汝同入賊軍，身死蠻徼，孤男稚女，艱食無告。

translations.literal: Zhu Second entered the bandit army with you and died on the barbarian frontier; orphaned boys and young girls eat bitterly with none to plead for them.
translations.idiomatic: Your brother Zhu Second went into the rebels with you and died on the frontier; his widow and children are destitute, with no one to help them.

sentences.zh: 汝未有恤孤之心，英特即有，諸無取也。

translations.literal: You have not the heart to succor orphans—if you are extraordinary, still do not take pride in it."
translations.idiomatic: You show no care for his orphans. Talent alone is nothing to boast of."

sentences.zh: 」 溫垂涕謝罪，即令召諸兄子皆至汴。

translations.literal: Wen shed tears and apologized, and at once ordered all his brothers’ sons summoned to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Wen wept and apologized, then had every nephew brought to Bian.

sentences.zh: 友寧、友倫皆立軍功，位至方鎮。）〉

translations.literal: Youning and Youlun both established military merit and reached posts as regional commissioners.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Youning and Youlun both won military honors and rose to govern provinces.)〉

sentences.zh: 元貞皇后張氏，乾化中追諡。

translations.literal: Empress Yuanzhen, née Zhang, was given a posthumous title in the Qianhua era.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuanzhen (Zhang) was posthumously honored during Qianhua.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》云：太祖皇后張氏早崩，開平二年，追封賢妃，至乾化二年十一月二十三日，追冊曰元貞皇后。

translations.literal: (《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: The Founder’s empress Zhang died early; in Kaiping year 2 she was posthumously enfeoffed as Worthy Consort; on the twenty-third day of the eleventh month of Qianhua year 2 she was posthumously invested as Empress Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records that Empress Zhang died young; in Kaiping 2 she was posthumously made Worthy Consort, and on 23 xi of month 11, Qianhua 2, was elevated to Empress Yuanzhen.

sentences.zh: 又，《北夢瑣言》云：梁祖魏國夫人張氏，碭山富室女，父蕤，曾為宋州刺史。

translations.literal: Moreover, 《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 says: The Liang Founder’s Lady of Wei, née Zhang, was daughter of a wealthy house in Dangshan; her father Rui had once been prefect of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Scattered Dreams of the Northern Quarter》 adds that Lady Zhang of Wei came from a rich Dangshan family; her father Rui had served as Songzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 溫時聞張有姿色，私心傾慕，有麗華之歎。

translations.literal: When Wen heard that Zhang had beauty, he secretly admired her and sighed with the lament of Lady Lihua.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Zhang’s beauty, Wen secretly yearned for her and sighed like a man longing for Lady Lihua.

sentences.zh: 及溫在同州，得張於兵間，因以婦禮納之。

translations.literal: When Wen was at Tongzhou he obtained Zhang amid the troops and took her in with the rites of a wife.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongzhou Wen took Zhang from among the captives and married her properly.

sentences.zh: 溫以其宿款，深加禮異。

translations.literal: Because of his long-standing affection, Wen treated her with deep courtesy and distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had loved her long before; he honored her with exceptional ceremony.

sentences.zh: 張賢明有禮，溫雖虎狼其心，亦所景伏。

translations.literal: Zhang was wise, clear, and observant of ritual; though Wen had the heart of a wolf or tiger, toward her he also bowed in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was intelligent and decorous; even Wen’s brutal nature bowed before her.

sentences.zh: 每軍謀國計，必先延訪。

translations.literal: Whenever there was military planning or state policy, he first extended invitation to consult her.
translations.idiomatic: On every matter of war or statecraft he consulted her first.

sentences.zh: 或已出師，中途有所不可，張氏一介請旋，如期而至，其信重如此。

translations.literal: Even after the army had marched out, if midway something could not proceed, Zhang with a single message would request return—and arrived on the appointed day; such was the trust placed in her.
translations.idiomatic: If a campaign had to be recalled mid-march, a single word from Zhang brought the army back on time—such was her authority.

sentences.zh: 初收兗、鄆，得朱瑾妻，溫告之曰：「彼既無依，寓於輜車。

translations.literal: When Yan and Yun were first taken, they obtained Zhu Jin’s wife; Wen told her: "She has no one to rely on—let her lodge in the baggage train."
translations.idiomatic: After the capture of Yan and Yun they took Zhu Jin’s wife; Wen said she was homeless and should travel in the supply train.

sentences.zh: 」張氏遣人召之，瑾妻再拜，張氏答拜泣下，謂之曰：「兗、鄆與司空同姓之國，昆仲之間，以小故尋戈，致吾姒如此。

translations.literal: Zhang sent someone to summon her; Jin’s wife bowed twice, Zhang returned the bow weeping, and said to her: "Yan and Yun are states of the same surname as the Minister of Works; between brothers a small quarrel drew swords, and my sister-in-law has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang sent for her; Jin’s wife bowed low, Zhang bowed back in tears and said: "Yan and Yun share our house’s surname—brothers quarreled over a trifle, and you, my sister-in-law, suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 設不幸汴州失守，妾亦似吾姒之今日也。

translations.literal: If by misfortune Bianzhou should fall, I too would be as my sister-in-law is today."
translations.idiomatic: Should Bian fall, I would share your fate."

sentences.zh: 」又泣下，乃度為尼，張恒給其費。

translations.literal: Again she wept, then had her tonsured as a nun; Zhang constantly supplied her expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping again, she had Jin’s wife take the veil and paid her upkeep.

sentences.zh: 張既卒，繼寵者非人，及僭號後，大縱朋淫，骨肉聚麀，帷薄荒穢，以致友珪之禍，起於婦人。

translations.literal: After Zhang died, those who succeeded her in favor were not worthy; after he assumed the imperial title he greatly indulged debauchery with companions, kin coupled like beasts, curtains and screens foul—so that Yougui’s disaster arose from a woman.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang’s death Wen’s favorites were unworthy; once emperor he plunged into orgies and incest until Yougui’s revolt—born of a woman’s grievance.

sentences.zh: 始能以柔婉之德，製豺虎之心，如張氏者，不亦賢乎！

translations.literal: To begin with, by gentle and yielding virtue to restrain the heart of wolf and tiger—as with Zhang—is she not worthy?
translations.idiomatic: At first, with soft grace she tamed a tiger’s heart—was Zhang not truly virtuous?

sentences.zh: 又，案《五代會要》所載，內職有梁太祖昭儀陳氏、昭容李氏，《歐陽史》並見《家人傳》。）〉

translations.literal: Moreover, examining what the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records, among inner offices were the Founder’s Lady of Bright Deportment Chen and Lady of Bright Countenance Li; both appear in 《Ouyang’s History》 in the Family Biographies.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 also lists the Founder’s Lady of Bright Deportment Chen and Lady of Bright Countenance Li, both noted in Ouyang Xiu’s 《New History》 Family section.)〉

sentences.zh: 末帝德妃張氏。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor’s Virtue Consort, née Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue Consort Zhang, consort of the Last Emperor.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》云：少帝妃張氏，乾化五年九月二十四日，冊為德妃，其夕薨。

translations.literal: (《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: The Young Emperor’s consort Zhang, on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month of Qianhua year 5, was invested as Virtue Consort; that very evening she died.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records that the Young Emperor’s consort Zhang was created Virtue Consort on 24 ix, Qianhua 5, and died the same night.

sentences.zh: 案《歐陽史次妃郭氏傳》云：晉天福三年，詔太社先藏罪人首級，許親屬收葬，乃出末帝首，遣右衛將軍安崇阮與妃同葬。

translations.literal: Examining 《Ouyang’s History》, in the biography of the second consort Guo it says: In Jin Tianfu year 3 an edict allowed kin to bury heads of criminals long stored at the Grand Altar; the Last Emperor’s head was produced, and Right Palace Guard general An Chongruan was sent to bury it together with the consort.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang’s 《History》 biography of Consort Guo notes that in Tianfu 3 Jin permitted families to claim criminals’ heads from the Grand Altar; the Last Emperor’s head was released and General An Chongruan buried it with his consort.

sentences.zh: 妃卒洛陽。

translations.literal: The consort died at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: She died at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 又案：《五代史》無外戚傳。

translations.literal: Moreover, examining: 《History of the Five Dynasties》 has no biography of maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: The 《History of the Five Dynasties》 contains no treatise on imperial in-laws.

sentences.zh: 《五代會要》云：梁太祖長女安陽公主，降羅廷規，開平二年八月追封。

translations.literal: 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: The Founder’s eldest daughter, Princess of Anyang, was married to Luo Tinggui and posthumously enfeoffed in Kaiping year 2, eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 lists the Founder’s eldest daughter, Princess Anyang, married to Luo Tinggui and posthumously enfeoffed in Kaiping 2, month 8.

sentences.zh: 長樂公主，降趙岩，開平元年五月十一日封。

translations.literal: Princess of Changle was married to Zhao Yan and enfeoffed on the eleventh day of the fifth month of Kaiping year 1.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Changle wed Zhao Yan and was enfeoffed on 11 v, Kaiping 1.

sentences.zh: 普寧公主，降昭祚王氏，開平元年五月十一日封。

translations.literal: Princess of Puning was married to Wang Zhaozuo and enfeoffed on the eleventh day of the fifth month of Kaiping year 1.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Puning wed Wang Zhaozuo on the same date, 11 v, Kaiping 1.

sentences.zh: 金華公主，開平二年十月封。

translations.literal: Princess of Jinhua was enfeoffed in the tenth month of Kaiping year 2.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jinhua was enfeoffed in month 10, Kaiping 2.

sentences.zh: 真寧公主，乾化三年十月五日封。

translations.literal: Princess of Zhenning was enfeoffed on the fifth day of the tenth month of Qianhua year 3.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Zhenning was enfeoffed on 5 x, Qianhua 3.

sentences.zh: 少帝長女壽春公主，乾化三年四月五日封。

translations.literal: The Young Emperor’s eldest daughter, Princess of Shouchun, was enfeoffed on the fifth day of the fourth month of Qianhua year 3.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Emperor’s eldest, Princess Shouchun, was enfeoffed on 5 iv, Qianhua 3.

sentences.zh: 第二女壽昌公主，貞明元年九月二十三日封。

translations.literal: His second daughter, Princess of Shouchang, was enfeoffed on the twenty-third day of the ninth month of Zhenming year 1.
translations.idiomatic: His second daughter, Princess Shouchang, was enfeoffed on 23 ix, Zhenming 1.

sentences.zh: 今考《通鑒考異》引《梁功臣列傳》云：羅廷規尚安陽公主，又尚金華公主。

translations.literal: Now examining 《Comprehensive Mirror: Collation of Variants》, which cites 《Biographies of Liang Meritorious Officials》: Luo Tinggui married Princess of Anyang and also married Princess of Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 collation cites the 《Biographies of Liang Meritorious Officials》: Luo Tinggui married both Princess Anyang and Princess Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 《薛史羅紹威傳》亦載開平四年，詔金華公主出家為尼。

translations.literal: 《Xue History》, biography of Luo Shaowei, also records that in Kaiping year 4 an edict had Princess of Jinhua leave the world and become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Old History》 biography of Luo Shaowei likewise records an edict in Kaiping 4 ordering Princess Jinhua to take the veil.

sentences.zh: 是金華公主實歸羅氏，而《五代會要》不載亦闕文也。）〉

translations.literal: Thus Princess of Jinhua in fact went to the Luo clan, while the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 does not record it—again a lacuna in the text.)〉
translations.idiomatic: So Jinhua truly married into the Luo house, though the 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 omits it—another gap in the record.)〉
